summary: Heartbeat probe drift between long-lived SSE clients and batch flushers causing opaque 429 bursts
description: Issue summary: BrightCart reports intermittent waves of 429s during peak traffic windows (03:15–03:35 UTC) that correlate with their long-lived SSE connections and a background batch-flush pipeline. Impact: Several storefront workers see 10–30% of streaming sessions rejected with 429s for short (~30s) pulses, causing user-visible refresh failures and increased retry noise. Environment: Dedicated pool (BrightCart dedicated lease) in prod-us-west, mixed traffic: persistent SSE sessions from browsers and periodic batch worker flushes that open/close short connections. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start 2k long-lived SSE sessions that send keepalive heartbeats every 30s. 2) Run batch flusher that issues 250 concurrent short POSTs every 15s. 3) Observe rate-limiter token-window and 429 count. Observed logs/metrics: - 429 spike timestamps: 2026-03-09T03:18:22Z, 03:21:07Z, 03:24:19Z - Token bucket utilization shows transient exhaustion of burst credits at the route layer for 8–12s windows. - Edge-proxy access logs show many keepalive probe requests counted as regular tokens (no special header) and concurrent short connections incrementing per-route counters. - Console quota view shows burst pool refill leveling that lags by ~10s relative to observed pulse. Expected behavior: Long-lived SSE heartbeats should either be accounted against a low-cost keepalive pool or excluded from burst accounting so short-lived high-concurrency flushes do not exhaust active burst credits. Customer expects guidance on configuration options and an actionable short-term workaround.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:03 UTC - BrightCart (Claire from BrightCart) - 'We're seeing sudden refresh failures on our product feed during the early-morning batch jobs. Looks like 429s spike for ~10 seconds and then recover. Can you help us tune rate limits?'

2026-03-10 09:18 UTC - Support (Aisha) - 'Thanks Claire — filing this internally. Can you confirm heartbeat frequency and whether the batch jobs originate from a single host or a pool? Also share any request IDs from a recent spike.'
2026-03-10 09:27 UTC - BrightCart (Claire) - 'Heartbeats: 30s. Batch flushers: 250 concurrent requests from 8 hosts. Example request-id: req_3f9a2e8c. We'll keep reproducing while you investigate.'

2026-03-11 14:06 UTC - Eng (Marco) - 'Seeing correlated token-bucket dips in metrics. Asking SRE to pull kube-proxy traces and edge logs. Temporary mitigation: enable isolated-burst-pool for their tenant and exempt known internal probe path — we can flip this from console if approved.'

2026-03-12 08:45 UTC - Support (Aisha) - 'Workaround available: enable split-burst-pool for BrightCart and set heartbeat path exemption. We need customer approval to apply tenant-level policy. Engineering patch to rate-limiter to ignore probe header is in review.'
investigation_notes: 03/10: Pulled token-bucket histogram for tenant brightcart-001; burst credits drop to 0 at the same 10s windows as 429 spikes.

Observed pattern: long-lived SSE sessions generate periodic HTTP GET keepalive probes that are currently accounted at full token cost by the route-layer limiter. When batch flushers start, their short-lived concurrent POSTs consume a large portion of the same burst pool causing immediate rejections for new streams.
Edge logs: several keepalive requests lack x-client-probe header; originates from customer SDK version 2.1.0 — recommend asking customer to upgrade to include probe header (opt-in) as short term.

Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rl/tenant-burst?orgId=1&var-tenant=brightcart-001 (snapshot id: s-20260310-burst), console trace link: https://console.redwood.ai/tenants/brightcart-001/requests?from=2026-03-09T03:10Z

Hypothesis: refill smoothing interval mismatch + shared burst pool for SSE and batch is causing transient starvation. Reproduced locally by running 2k SSE clients + periodic batch fanout; replicated 429 pulses after ~18 minutes of run time on medium-sized dedicated pool.
Temporary mitigation tested in staging: enabling isolated-burst-pool for SSE (separate token bucket) eliminated 429 pulses in reproduce run; CPU/throughput unaffected.
resolution: Workaround provided: (1) Applied temporary tenant policy to split burst pools (SSE vs batch) for BrightCart and enabled heartbeat-path exemption on 2026-03-12 09:12 UTC. (2) Recommended customer upgrade SDK to include x-client-probe header to avoid full-cost accounting for keepalives. Engineering: rate-limiter PR #858 (ignore x-client-probe when present) merged to staging; rollout to prod planned after one-day soak. Follow-ups: - Product task to add 'split burst pool' toggle in Console (P0 product ticket). - Engineering to add metrics for 'probe-exempted tokens' to console and alerting.
